items.headline: GAP NOW CLOSED — Thursday was a MINER BREAKDOWN that no agent captured: GDX -2.96%, Newmont -3.10%, Pan American -9.70%, on a day gold fell only 1.03%
items.summary: These figures come from the new deterministic price spine (scripts/price-spine.js), not from an agent reading a news page — Yahoo's chart endpoint, validated on 24 of 24 closes that were independently verified this week from unrelated sources. THURSDAY 13 AUG: GDX 88.27 (-2.96%), SILJ 29.44 (-2.39%), Newmont 114.19 (-3.10%), Barrick 43.81 (-1.95%), Pan American 47.30 (-9.70%). Against that, gold front-month fell just 1.03% to 4,363.60 and silver front-month 1.04% to 64.873. So THE MINERS UNDERPERFORMED THE METAL BY ROUGHLY 2-3x IN A SINGLE SESSION. FRIDAY 14 AUG partially retraced: GDX 89.97 (+1.93%), SILJ 29.86 (+1.43%), Newmont 117.76 (+3.13%), Barrick 44.00 (+0.43%), Pan American 47.42 (+0.25%) while gold rose 0.39% to 4,380.40. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: the -9.70% Pan American figure exactly reproduces a claim made by one of the verification agents that was cut off mid-run, and WTI's $81.25/$82.40 settles likewise — two separate pipelines agreeing to the cent. CONTEXT that makes Thursday worse: it was the week's RISK-ON day, with the S&P closing at a record on soft PPI. The miners broke down anyway. ── THE FUNDAMENTALS SAY THE OPPOSITE, which is the tension worth holding. Barricks own release (10 Aug): gold cost of sales $1,993/oz vs $1,654 (+20.5%) and AISC $1,866 vs $1,684 (+10.8%) — but realised gold $4,417/oz vs $3,295 (+34.1%) outran both, so AISC margin per ounce went $1,611 -> $2,551, i.e. +58.3%. Costs rose and unit margin EXPANDED. Pan American reiterated full-year cost guidance, grew net earnings 61% to $305m, generated $344m of attributable FCF (+47%) and returned a record $300m — its miss was tax ($179m charge) and gold volumes, not economics.
items.actionable: This materially changes the miner read and cuts against the 'margins are expanding' conclusion drawn from Barrick's and Pan American's own filings. Pan American -9.70% is the market's verdict on its Q2 tax charge and gold-volume miss, delivered the day after the release, and it swamped the reiterated cost guidance. More importantly the whole complex fell 2-3x the metal's decline on a record-high day for the S&P — that is the miner sleeve failing its own leverage test in the direction that hurts. Friday's bounce recovered roughly two-thirds of GDX's drop but Pan American recovered almost none of its. Hold both facts at once: the filings show unit margins expanding while the tape marked the whole complex down 2-3x the metal. When fundamentals and price disagree this sharply in one session, the tape is usually telling you about positioning and fund flows, not about mine economics.

items.headline: SILVER, the book's largest risk: three sessions of failed breakouts. It never printed a 67 handle, made two successively lower highs after Wednesday's peak, and closed Friday $64.68 — up just 1.74% on the week
items.summary: Spot silver has no official settlement, so these are read daily-table closes, corrected against two feeds. INVESTING.COM XAG/USD daily table: Fri 7 Aug 63.5766 (high 65.1620); Wed 12 Aug 65.3250 (HIGH 66.8170); Thu 13 Aug 64.4800 (high 66.3124, -1.29%); Fri 14 Aug 64.6819 (high 65.7150, +0.31%). COMEX Sep-26 futures for cross-check: Wed 65.700 (high 66.980), Thu 64.993, Fri 65.108. BASELINE RECONCILIATION: Wednesday's 65.3250 matches the independently verified Wednesday baseline to the cent and matches a third source's 13 Aug report ($64.48, 'down $0.84', implying a 65.32 prior) — Wednesday is anchored on three feeds. THE STRUCTURE IS THE STORY. The intraday highs run 66.8170 (Wed) → 66.3124 (Thu) → 65.7150 (Fri): two successively lower highs. Silver never traded with a 67 handle in spot at any point. And the Wednesday high was made BEFORE the 08:30 ET CPI release, not on it. WEEKLY MOVE, corrected: 64.6819 vs the prior Friday's 63.5766 = +1.74%, not the +2.4% derived elsewhere.
items.actionable: At 1.6x the week was +2.78% on the levered position — positive, but by less than a glance at the closes suggests, and the internal structure deteriorated across all three sessions. The pattern now has three instances: silver rallies into a catalyst, makes its high at or before the release, and bleeds afterwards. Metal that cannot hold gains on friendly news (in-line CPI Wednesday, soft PPI Thursday) is the signal, not the plus sign on the week. Watch whether it can clear 66.82 — until then each rally is a lower high.

items.headline: The week delivered NO net duration relief: the 10Y round-tripped to exactly 4.68% and the 30Y closed 5.25% — and a correction, the 30Y has NOT broken out, the 2026 peak is 5.27% set 31 July
items.summary: VERIFIED AGAINST TWO OFFICIAL SOURCES: the US Treasury daily par yield curve CSV, cross-checked against the Federal Reserve H.15 release dated 14 Aug. CLOSES (Treasury par curve, ~3:30pm ET bid-side): Wed 12 Aug 2Y 4.20 / 10Y 4.68 / 30Y 5.24. Thu 13 Aug 2Y 4.15 / 10Y 4.63 / 30Y 5.21. Fri 14 Aug 2Y 4.17 / 10Y 4.68 / 30Y 5.25. H.15 independently reproduces 12 and 13 Aug exactly; it carries no 14 Aug row (it publishes a day in arrears), so Friday rests on the Treasury curve alone. ARITHMETIC: Thursday rallied 10Y -5bp / 30Y -3bp on soft PPI, then Friday gave it all back, 10Y +5bp / 30Y +4bp. Net across both sessions the 10Y round-tripped to its Wednesday level. THE CORRECTION TO OUR OWN NARRATIVE: we have been describing the 30Y as breaking out to post-2007 highs. It has not. The 2026 maximum is 5.27%, set 31 JULY — a unique print. Friday's 5.25% is 2bp below it and merely matches the 10 Aug local high. Over 22 Jul-14 Aug the 30Y ranged 5.09-5.27, an 18bp band. THE TWO AUCTIONS: Wednesday's $42bn 10-year stopped at 4.683%, the highest clear since Aug 2007, with a 2.53 cover and dealers left only 8.6%. Thursday's $25bn 30-year (verified field-by-field from the TreasuryDirect PDF, CUSIP 912810UW6) stopped at 5.216%, the highest 30Y clear since 2001, with a 0.4bp tail, 2.39 cover and indirects at 66.85%, in line with their ~67% average. September is priced roughly 69% hold.
items.actionable: Two things to hold at once. The good news is that 'the 30Y is accelerating to post-2007 highs' was wrong — it peaked on 31 July and has chopped sideways since, which is a materially less hostile backdrop for the S-REITs and developers than we have been describing. The bad news is that a week containing an in-line CPI, a soft PPI and two orderly auctions produced ZERO net duration relief. Both auctions cleared at multi-decade high yields with demand present, so this is a term-premium problem, not a buyers' strike. Do not publish or act on a 5.27% vendor print as a new high.

items.headline: The US week in two halves: a RECORD S&P close Thursday on soft PPI, then Friday's double miss — retail sales -0.6% and sentiment down to 51.0
items.summary: AP syndicated recap, page stamp Thu 13 Aug 4:21pm ET, ~20 minutes after the cash close. CLOSES: S&P 500 7,798.99 (+50.49); Dow 53,839.99 (+69.72); Nasdaq Composite 26,803.03 (+214.54); Russell 2000 3,052.85 (+7.36). VERIFICATION, pinned from BOTH sides: 7,798.99 - 50.49 = 7,748.50, matching the verified Wednesday S&P close TO THE CENT; and Friday's separate recap gives 7,785.76 - 13.23 = 7,798.99, EXACT. Dow, Nasdaq and Russell all reconcile the same way in both directions. THE DATA: July PPI for final demand UNCHANGED (0.0%) m/m against +0.2% consensus; +4.7% y/y against 4.9% expected. Composition: final demand GOODS -0.7%, services +0.2%, construction +2.2%, with the goods decline driven by energy -3.1% and foods -0.9% — which substantiates rather than assumes the softer-oil read. ONE HOT LINE: core PPI +4.2% y/y actually beat the 4.1% consensus, and because bls.gov returned 403 the core figures rest on secondary sources. Jobless claims 209,000, up 9,000, against 202,000 expected. Semiconductors led (Sandisk +15%, Micron strong). ── THEN FRIDAY REVERSED THE MOOD. Both landed Friday 14 Aug — retail sales 08:30 ET, UMich 10:00 ET. RETAIL SALES (Census advance report): July retail and food services $763.6bn, -0.6% m/m against consensus +0.1%, the sharpest monthly decline since May 2025; +5.0% y/y. Ex-autos -0.3% (cons. +0.2%); ex-autos-and-gas -0.2% (cons. +0.3%). THE CONTROL GROUP — which strips autos, gasoline, building materials and food services and feeds the PCE line of GDP — fell 0.4% against consensus +0.3%, after a revised +0.4% in June. So this was NOT a volatile-category artifact. Drivers: motor vehicles -1.8%, nonstore/online -2.2% (Prime Day fell in June this year), gasoline stations -0.9%. UMICH preliminary August: headline 51.0 against consensus 54.5 (one source prints 55.0) and a July final of 55.2. THE CROSS-CURRENT FOR METALS: year-ahead inflation expectations ROSE to 4.3% even as sentiment fell. FRIDAY CLOSES, chain-reconciled to the verified Wednesday baseline with zero residual: S&P 500 7,785.76 (-13.23, -0.17%); Dow 53,732.41 (-107.58, -0.20%); Nasdaq Composite 26,729.16 (-73.86, -0.28%); Russell 2000 3,068.42 (+15.57, +0.51%) at a fresh record on its fourth straight up day. VIX made its lowest CLOSE of 2026 at 14.25 (lowest of the year, not an all-time low).
items.actionable: Two consecutive benign inflation prints plus a soft-side claims number are what pushed September hike odds lower and drove the record close — the disinflation leg supporting both the equity book and the rate-sensitive precious-metals complex. Use 7,798.99 as Thursday's mark, not the unconfirmed 7,800 intraday print. But note what it did NOT do: silver made a lower high on this session and the long end gave the whole rally back on Friday. The week's clearest negative surprise, and it argues against reading Thursday's soft PPI as a clean soft landing. A negative control group — the GDP-relevant cut — alongside sentiment at 51.0 is a growth signal to weigh against the cyclical side of the book: the Singapore banks, the developers and the oil sleeve. Do not frame Friday as risk-off, though: breadth was positive, the Russell closed at a record and the VIX made its lowest close of the year. The consumer weakened; the market did not panic.

items.headline: TENCENT: Q2 revenue beat but IFRS profit was flat and free cash flow went negative for the first time since 2005 — the stock fell 4.46% Thursday to HK$441.00, then steadied at HK$440.00
items.summary: THE RESULTS, verified against Tencent's own PR Newswire release stamped 12 Aug 18:29 CST — 2.5 hours AFTER the Wednesday HK close, so the reaction is Thursday's. Revenue RMB204,785m, +11% y/y (beat); gross profit RMB118.4bn +13% (margin 58% vs 57%); operating profit RMB67.3bn IFRS +12%; profit attributable to equity holders RMB56,022m IFRS, +0.7% — flat, and roughly 9% below consensus; non-IFRS RMB68.4bn +9%, which is ON consensus (RMB68.2bn expected). SEGMENTS: domestic games RMB47.3bn +17%; international games RMB18.6bn -0.8% reported (+4% constant currency); marketing services RMB43.6bn +22%; FinTech & Business Services RMB60.3bn +9%. Arithmetic checks: 47.3+18.6+32.5 = 98.4, exactly the stated VAS line. THE AI DRAG, QUANTIFIED BY THE COMPANY ITSELF: operating profit EXCLUDING New AI Products was RMB86.1bn, +19%. Capex rose 176% y/y to RMB52.8bn and free cash flow turned NEGATIVE for the first time since 2005. THE PRICE CHAIN, verified and corrected (the Thursday close is HK$441.00, not the HK$441.40 circulating): Wed 461.60 (-1.95%) → Thu 441.00 (-20.60, -4.46%) → Fri 440.00 (-1.00, -0.23%). Arithmetic: 441.00/461.60-1 = -4.463%; 440.00/441.00-1 = -0.227%. Both print exactly as reported. Cumulative Wed-to-Fri: -4.68%. Primary source is a Hong Kong close report published 16:17 HKT, 17 minutes after the close.
items.actionable: Mark Tencent at HK$440.00. Read the result the right way round before acting: demand is genuinely fine — revenue beat, marketing services +22%, domestic games +17% — and the adjusted profit line analysts actually model came in on consensus. What changed is the cash profile. Capex +176% and negative free cash flow for the first time in twenty-one years means Tencent is now spending through a capex cycle rather than harvesting one. That is a re-rating question, not a demand question, and the market took 4.7% off over two sessions to price it.

This is the book's live event risk for tomorrow.

items.headline: SMIC is the book's standout: Q2 profit +261.7% y/y, and the stock rose 4.81% to HK$70.80 on Friday AGAINST a -1.77% Hang Seng Tech tape
items.summary: TIMING: SMIC disclosed Q2 AFTER the Thursday 13 Aug HK close, so the reaction is FRIDAY. THE NUMBERS: revenue $3.01bn, +36.1% y/y; profit attributable to shareholders $479.2m, +261.7% y/y; gross margin 25.3% against 20.4% a year earlier; wafer shipments +20.1% y/y; utilisation 93.7% against 92.5%. Q3 guidance: revenue +2% to +4% q/q, gross margin 26-28%. THE BEAT IS AGAINST THE COMPANY'S OWN GUIDANCE: prior guidance was +14-16% q/q revenue and 20-22% GM, against actual +20% q/q and 25.3%. PRICE, verified three ways: HK$70.80, +3.25, +4.81% (Trading Economics, stamped 'this Friday August 14th'); The Standard's close-of-session report stamped 14-08-2026 16:35 HKT says SMIC 'up 4.8 percent'; a third close flash gives +4.81%. Arithmetic: 70.80 - 3.25 = HK$67.55 implied Thursday close. CAVEAT: that HK$67.55 Thursday close is DERIVED from a quote page's previous-close field, not read from a close report.
items.actionable: SMIC carries HK$70.80 into Monday and is the best-performing name in the book this week. It rose 4.8% on a session when Hang Seng Tech fell 1.77% and peer Hua Hong fell 11.55% DESPITE its own beat — so this is company-specific execution, not a sector bid, and the divergence is the point. Q3 gross margin guided higher again to 26-28% after a quarter that beat the company's own 20-22% guide. This is the one HK position where the news flow is unambiguously working.

Your sleeve did not move as one: Tencent and Xiaomi were marked down while SMIC rose 4.8%. Note the A-share detail that matters for the miners — precious-metals shares were notable losers onshore on Thursday.

items.headline: UNPRICED, AND IT MEETS THIS MORNING'S OPEN: China's July new yuan loans posted a RECORD 340bn contraction against +45bn expected — released after Friday's HK close
items.summary: Released Friday 14 Aug (page stamped 05:32 ET); all figures read verbatim. New yuan loans CONTRACTED 340bn yuan ($50.43bn) in July — the second contraction of 2026 after April, and the largest monthly contraction ON RECORD — against a Reuters poll of +45bn and June's +1.61trn. ARITHMETIC: the miss against consensus is 385bn yuan; the month-on-month swing is -1.95trn. Household loans including mortgages -460.3bn after +264.6bn in June; corporate loans -130bn after +1.5trn. NOTE the components sum to -590.3bn, roughly 250bn MORE negative than the -340bn headline; the gap is bill financing and non-bank lending, so the figures are consistent rather than contradictory. M2 +7.7% y/y against 7.9% consensus, down from 8.0%. Outstanding TSF +7.4% y/y, unchanged. The PBOC said it would maintain an 'appropriately loose' stance and 'roll out practical, effective measures as needed', without detail. SEPARATELY: July activity data did NOT print Thursday or Friday — the NBS calendar confirms it is due TODAY, Monday 17 Aug, 10:00 Beijing.
items.actionable: This is the live catalyst for your HK sleeve this morning. A record loan contraction plus an M2 miss is the strongest China easing signal in months, and because it landed after Friday's close it is UNPRICED — it meets Monday's open together with the July activity dump due 10:00 Beijing. Two-sided: it is bad growth news but raises the odds of stimulus, and Hong Kong is already at a three-week low after four down sessions.

items.headline: SINGAPORE: read the bank prices carefully today (DBS's drop was the dividend, OCBC goes ex this morning) — and UOL's -8.75% is the one real loss

The Wednesday row of 5,720.75 / -0.58% matches the verified baseline to the decimal, validating the table as a genuine cash-index series. Two-session net +22.84 points, +0.40%. That is 1.06% of the Thursday close against an observed -1.07% — so the underlying stock was FLAT on Friday, not down. OCBC's ex-date is TODAY, Monday 17 Aug, 47 cents, paid 28 Aug — roughly 1.48% mechanical. ── THE REST OF THE SLEEVE SPLIT VIOLENTLY ON RESULTS. UOL: Wed 10.17 (+2.42%); THU 9.55 (-6.10%, open 10.18, high 10.20, low 9.44, vol 5.43M); FRI 9.28 (-2.83%, high 9.60, low 9.11). Arithmetic: Thu -0.62 on 10.17 = -6.096%; Fri -0.27 on 9.55 = -2.827%; two-day 9.28/10.17-1 = -8.751%. Two independent post-close quote feeds confirm both session dates. CRITICALLY: there is no dividend, ex-date or corporate action to excuse this — the results wire declares no dividend, and Thursday OPENED one cent ABOVE the prior close before collapsing intraday. The trigger is a 7% revenue decline masked by fair-value gains. CITY DEVELOPMENTS rose 4.33% Thursday on tripled profit plus a strategic review. SINGTEL: Wed 4.290, Thu 4.250 (-0.93%), Fri 4.450 (+4.71%). Its 1QFY2027 update was released PRE-OPEN Thursday; the market sold the -71.6% headline down to 4.190 intraday, then reversed once the underlying +21% / S$831m — an 11.4% consensus beat — was digested. Publish +4.71% to S$4.450, the close, NOT the +3.5% intraday figure still in the wire copy.
items.actionable: Across DBS (ex Friday) and OCBC (ex today) your two bank lines show a combined ~2.5% of purely mechanical decline in consecutive sessions. Use S$31.32 as OCBC's ex-adjusted reference, not the S$31.79 close. If the P&L feed marks DBS to 75.53 without accruing the S$0.81 receivable, the book understates DBS by ~1.06% until 25 August. The inverse error is the dangerous one: if a genuine bank selloff coincides with today's ex-date, do not write it off as 'just the dividend'. UOL is the genuine damage in the Singapore book — -8.75% across two sessions with nothing mechanical to explain it, on a 7% revenue decline masked by fair-value gains. Mark it as a real loss, unlike the two bank moves. Singtel is the mirror image: a headline-driven overreaction that fully reversed within a session, which is worth remembering the next time a -71.6% figure appears in a results headline.

items.actionable: Retire the stale-feed alert permanently — this was a misreading of tick size, not a data fault, and no vendor swap is needed. The useful inversion: because one tick is 0.5-0.85% on these names, any sub-0.5% non-zero change reported on them IS a genuine data error and should be treated as suspect. Mapletree Logistics is the one actually grinding lower — down every session from 1.200 to 1.170, -2.5% across the week.

items.headline: July CPI landed exactly on consensus — 3.4% headline / 2.5% core — and September hike odds fell about 10 points to ~38%
items.summary: Read directly off the BLS release, USDL-26-1378, embargo stamp 'until 8:30 a.m. (ET) Wednesday, August 12, 2026'. THE PRINT: headline CPI-U +0.1% m/m SA (after -0.4% in June), +3.4% y/y NSA (after +3.5%); core +0.2% m/m (after 0.0%), +2.5% y/y (after +2.6%). Both y/y prints matched consensus exactly. Shelter contributed roughly two-thirds of the entire monthly gain. PRECISION NOTE: the BLS release carries no consensus figures, so 'in line' is verified only for the two y/y numbers. MARKET RESPONSE: CME FedWatch at 11:32 a.m. ET showed ~62% for a HOLD at 3.50-3.75% in September against ~38% for a hike, versus ~52/48 the prior day. TIMING CORRECTION: hike odds FELL through the morning and did not recover — a 42.1% reading circulating from 08:52 a.m. ET is an early-morning figure, not a closing one. Every FedWatch number here is INTRADAY. FRAMING THE BOOK MUST NOT GET BACKWARDS: this FOMC is debating a HIKE, not a cut. There is no cut in the September distribution.
items.actionable: A hike deferred is direct financing-cost relief on the 1.6x margin-levered silver leg and removes the tail that mattered most to it. Same direction for the miners and for the Mapletree/Keppel complex, where SGD rates track USD. By Friday, September was priced roughly 69% hold — the dovish shift held all week even as the long end refused to rally.

items.headline: Gold closed Wednesday at $4,406 (+0.87%), its best close in two months — and oil settled DEAD FLAT despite the largest EIA crude build since January 2023
items.summary: GOLD, verified across three independently opened pages: spot $4,406.20, +0.90% (Kitco PM report, 'late-afternoon U.S. trading Wednesday'), with a second wrap giving identical figures. ANCHOR ARITHMETIC — the strongest reconciliation of the batch: Kitco's intraday pair $4,435.58 at +1.54% implies a Tuesday close of $4,368.31 against our reference $4,368.04-4,368.29, a TWO-CENT match. Computed off $4,368.29: close +$37.91 = +0.868%; session high $4,438.30 = +1.603%. Gold retained 54% of its peak gain and gave back $32.10 from the high — and its Wednesday high topped Tuesday's by only ~$3, inside the disagreement between two feeds on the same datum. OIL: Brent front-month settled Wed $88.98 (+0.08%) and WTI $83.27 (+0.08%) — both +7 cents. The 11 Aug rows read $88.91 and $83.20, matching our Tuesday reference settles to the cent, and the 10 Aug Brent row reads $87.72, exactly the corrected Monday settle established after our $87.85 spot/CFD error. Three consecutive reference marks reproduced. THE EIA NUMBER, verified by downloading the Weekly Petroleum Status Report PDF: commercial crude ex-SPR rose 17.4mb to 424.4mb for the week ending 7 Aug, against a consensus DRAW of 1.4mb — an ~18.8mb miss and the largest build since January 2023. Yet crude is still ~2% BELOW the five-year average, and imports jumped 1.14 mbpd week-on-week, which alone accounts for roughly 8mb of the build.
items.actionable: On oil, the headline number is worse than the tape and the tape is right: a 17.4mb build producing a +7-cent settle says the market wrote it off as a trade-flow artifact of the Hormuz disruption rather than genuine oversupply. Do not read it as bearish for the USO/XLE leg. NOTE THE GAP: no verified Thursday or Friday settles for Brent or WTI, and no verified Thu/Fri gold close — those verification agents were cut off mid-run.
